findings.summary: The incorporated prose and ratified policy add the missing sanitized-real classes and lifecycle, but the mandatory executable privacy closure is not fail-closed and therefore does not fully resolve PRIV-G2-R2-001. The bound `sanitizedRealDecision` never enforces exactly 20 prompt artifacts; its direct-identifier implementation recognizes only email, SSN-like, and phone patterns plus the single literal named entity `Ada Lovelace`, although the policy also prohibits postal address, precise location, government/account/customer/employee/device identifiers, IP/MAC, identity-bearing URLs, biometrics, signatures, secrets, tokens, credentials, and free-text self-identification; and its raw-disposition check accepts any signed receipt with a nonempty copy-ID list without binding those copies to the source, corpus, or complete copy inventory. Independently resealed counterexamples using the exact target-bound oracle returned `ACCEPT` for a five-prompt corpus, postal address text, an IPv4 address, an API secret/token, and an unrelated raw-copy receipt. The 15 declared sanitized-real fixtures contain only one email direct-identifier mutation and no exact-count or category-complete negative matrix, so the bundled suite can report `SANITIZED_REAL_OK` while violating the Exam and policy. The same validator is also hard-bound to the superseded base Exam digest and terminates with a digest assertion when run against this round-three target, so it cannot produce a complete passing target-revision result as currently bound.
findings.requiredResolution: Make the target-bound sanitized-real oracle enforce exactly the 20 manifest-bound prompt objects and closed, duplicate-free artifact/derivative inventories; validate the provenance, use authorization, sanitizer and independent-inspector identities/revisions, policy and target digests, raw working-copy inventory, per-copy disposition receipts, encrypted corpus/version/key, and every production-versus-fixture credential and destination as one coherently bound record graph. Replace the narrow hard-coded identifier checks with a revision-bound deterministic detector/oracle and negative fixtures for every prohibited direct-identifier and free-text category, plus category boundary and evasion cases. Recompute linkage results from the frozen authorized source pool rather than accepting claimed trials, and bind each raw receipt one-to-one to the complete authorized inventory. Add exact-count, missing/extra/duplicate prompt, source-pool substitution, receipt substitution, partial inventory, detector/normalization drift, and cross-destination counterexamples. Make the validator runnable and digest-bound to the final canonical Exam revision, refresh every affected digest, and obtain a new independent exact-revision Privacy review.

escalations.reason: PRIV-G2-R2-001 remains an unresolved major Exam-adequacy finding because the exact target-bound privacy oracle accepts records that violate the ratified sanitized-real policy and can still report its declared matrix green. The default-closed policy requires human Privacy specialist escalation unless a revised exact target closes the executable gap; this reviewer cannot accept or waive it.

A false privacy acceptance can place identifiable or secret originator-derived prompt material into Git history, provider copies, caches, indexes, exports, and backups, creating durable propagation and material privacy-rights impact. No such risk acceptance or disposition is authorized by this review.
